name: Les Halos de Jupiter Châteauneuf-du-Pape Adrastee 2016
text:
## Les Halos de Jupiter Châteauneuf-du-Pape Adrastée 2016

**The story.** Les Halos de Jupiter, named for the planet and its rings, began with the 2007 vintage as a partnership between the celebrated consultant Philippe Cambie and Michel Gassier, owner of Château de Nages in the Costières de Nîmes. Cambie, "the giant of Châteauneuf du Pape", as Jeff Leve calls him, died in December 2021 aged 59, leaving a lasting mark on the many southern Rhône estates he advised ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). Les Halos de Jupiter makes wines across the southern Rhône, from Costières de Nîmes and Côtes du Rhône to Rasteau, Gigondas, Vacqueyras and [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC).

**The wine: Adrastée.** Adrastée is the top cuvée: 100% old-vine [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) from vines over 100 years old in the famous [La Crau](https://www.google.com/maps?q=La+Crau,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) lieu-dit, not far from Vieux Télégraphe's vines. The grapes are fully destemmed without crushing, fermented for about five weeks at 28°C and aged 12 months in one-year-old French oak barrels; only about 125 cases are made ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/); [Mövenpick, technical sheet](https://www.moevenpick-wein.com/fr/customization_catalog/product/pdf/product_id/95814/file/2016-adrastee-chateauneuf-du-pape-aop-halos-de-jupiter.pdf), in French).

**The vintage.** 2016 is one of the great modern years in the southern Rhône. [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) quotes [Michel Chapoutier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier) saying it could be better than the legendary 1990: warm conditions and reduced yields gave wines of great concentration, "certainly one of the great vintages" for reds, and safe for cellaring into the 2030s.

**What the critics say for 2016.**
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 98** (as listed by the Swiss merchant [Mövenpick](https://www.moevenpick-wein.com/fr/customization_catalog/product/pdf/product_id/95814/file/2016-adrastee-chateauneuf-du-pape-aop-halos-de-jupiter.pdf)), which also gives its own 19.5/20. The merchant describes black berries, lavender and herbes de Provence with delicate toast; rich, creamy and juicy, with "stunning" concentration of cassis, blackberry and stewed plum and an almost endless finish.
- **Jeff Leve, [The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/): 93** (December 2021). "Rich, full and lush", concentrated with ripe, sweet, pure raspberries, red and black cherries, thyme and flowers; "already drinking well, so if you have a bottle, or two, there is no need to hesitate."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 90.1** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2026 to 2033, and Mövenpick says to 2032. Leve says Halos de Jupiter is usually best 4 to 15 years after the vintage. So it is in its prime now. Serve at about 15.5°C and decant about an hour ahead ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**Food.** Leve suggests classic meat dishes, from veal and lamb to duck, game and cassoulet, plus hearty fish like tuna and mushroom dishes ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). My picks: rack of lamb with herbes de Provence, or duck breast with cherries.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Adrastée, which is very hard to find.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k); his successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) built the summer castle that gave Châteauneuf-du-Pape, "the Pope's new castle", its name ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Local growers led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) of [Château Fortia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Fortia) drew up France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules in 1923, made law in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune; the decree is still in force ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Jupiter's halos.** The estate takes its name from the planet [Jupiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupiter) and its halos ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/les-halos-de-jupiter-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).
